key_insight: Riemannian Anderson mixing accelerates natural-gradient optimization on neural Wasserstein manifolds by reusing past residuals without forming Hessians.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a way to reduce training iterations for probability-measure optimization in sampling, inverse problems, and generative modeling.
method: Represent probability measures as neural-network pushforwards of a reference distribution.
Equip network parameters with a pullback Wasserstein metric and interpret natural-gradient updates as fixed-point iterations.
Apply Riemannian Anderson mixing using historical residuals to capture approximate second-order information.
evidence_signal: Across multimodal sampling, PDE inverse problems, aggregation dynamics, Bayesian logistic regression, and generative modeling, the abstract reports fewer natural-gradient iterations and competitive gradient-evaluation counts and wall-clock time relative to SGD and Adam.
watch_item: Practical gains may depend on the cost and numerical stability of the point-dependent metric and residual-history computations.
paper_title: Fixed-point acceleration on Neural Wasserstein manifolds
